text:
julia: Heads up — onboarding script in our CI broke on a fresh Debian image when running `apt install redwoodctl` then `redwoodctl login --profile=ci`. It aborts with a write error to $HOME/.config even though the container mounts the repo as root-owned.

julia: Error snippet: 

error: saving profile failed: open /repo/.config/redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
failed to write atomically: permission denied

rahul: We hit similar in ephemeral runners. Workarounds: set XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a tmp dir or `mkdir -p /tmp/redwood && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/redwood redwoodctl login`. But that's not intuitive.

omar: Another annoyance — device-code auth often times out in headless CI. The default device TTL (60s) is too short for copy/paste workflows or for human-in-the-loop demos. When it expires the CLI exits with non-retryable error.

julia: Example flow output: 

Visit https://auth.redwood.ai/device and enter code: Z9Y8-X7W6
Waiting for authorization...
error: device code expired

nico: Two proposed CLI UX fixes: (1) on unwritable config dir detect EACCES and print a single-line suggestion: "set XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/path or use --profile-path /path" plus a CI-friendly exit code; (2) add `--device-ttl-seconds` and `--headless-token PATH` so CI can supply a pre-generated token path. Also consider printing a fallback: "using in-memory profile; run `redwoodctl persist --path /tmp/token` to save."

rahul: For install pain, some distros install redwoodctl binary with root:root and /usr/local/bin symlink that resolves to an rpm-maintained path. If user's HOME is mounted read-only the CLI shouldn't attempt atomic rename; fallback to write-temp-then-move or write-per-user under /tmp.

omar: Could we detect container contexts (CI env vars like CI=1, GITHUB_ACTIONS) and switch to non-atomic safe write mode automatically? That would avoid a loud error during onboarding.

julia: I can repro with a tiny Dockerfile, will attach in the GH issue. Snippet: 

FROM debian:12
RUN groupadd -g 1000 repo && useradd -m -u 1001 dev 
USER dev
WORKDIR /repo
COPY . /repo
ENV HOME=/home/dev
CMD ["/bin/sh","-c","redwoodctl login --profile=ci"]

ci-bot: (automated) job #1024 failed: onboarding-e2e  auth: permission denied while writing profile. Logs: https://ci.internal/job/1024

nico: I'll file a minimal GH issue with suggested UX strings and a unit test case that stubs an EACCES on config dir. Also adding a note to docs: "CI-friendly auth" with example `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `--headless-token`.

julia: Thanks — for short-term releng fix I'll update the onboarding script to export XDG_CONFIG_HOME into a writable tmp dir. But long-term we should make redwoodctl gentler in ephemeral environments.
